_doc: Round 10 violin per-note table (size 1): gain_db = dB on each partial's output gain (index 0 = the fundamental); dark_db = dB added to each partial's onset darkening (decaying as exp(-t/ob_s), negative brightens; 48 partials, the last held above); the scalars replace the global for that note (round 10 adds hiss_db, dB on the hiss, and a0_db, the air mode's level). Read at note-on by the nearest MIDI note; none outside first..last. Round 11: rs0_db, rs1_db, rs2_db (45 each): the residual layers' spectra, dB of band energy in look.py's 1/6-octave bands (80 Hz-16 kHz, the 45 with STFT bins) as the score's STFT (2048 Hann) reads them, at an envelope of 1, in the twin's output units (-200 = off): rs0 the sustain's noise, rs1 the onset's, rs2 the release's. Round 12: kv_su [8][4]: dB on each partial's gain by octave column (centres 110 Hz x 2^k, interpolated in log frequency over the partials, held past the ends) at su_t = 1.0, 1.9, 2.8, 3.7 s from the note-on, held before the first and after the last (the release too): the held note's level over time, its mean over 1.5-3.5 s 0. kv_on [8][6] (dB at 0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.35, 0.6 s; 0 at 0.9 s and after) and kv_rl [8][5] (dB at 0.05, 0.15, 0.3, 0.45, 0.6 s after the let-go; 0 at the let-go, the last held): the partials' onset and release envelope by octave column (the cello's kn_on / kn_rl, by the violin table's weight). rk_on [3 layers][6] and rk_rl [3][5]: the same knots' envelope (dB, amplitude) on each residual layer (rs0 sustain, rs1 onset, rs2 release; rk_on of rs2 and rk_rl of rs1 are 0). slow_db is 0.35 x round 11's.
